tonight.headline: Four Jaguars at Denver. The Golden swap makes it three.
body: Week 2 has not started. ESPN has KEI returns 118.1 to your 114.5 and gives you 48%. Your lineup starts Lawrence, Tuten, Cam Little and the Jaguars defense, all in the same game at Denver.

Nothing here is urgent tonight except the Coker check after 01:00. The one lineup move is Golden into the flex for Tuten before Sunday 11:00, which takes a starter out of the Denver game and puts in a receiver who drew 12 targets in Week 1.

case.label: What their lineup depends on
case.body: KEI returns start Jaxson Dart and Cam Skattebo, both Giants, both at the Rams on Monday night: Dart threw three touchdowns in Week 1 and Skattebo ran 18 times for 81 and a score. De'Von Achane, their other back, goes to San Francisco, whose defense NBC ranks in its top tier.

case.label: What your stack depends on
case.body: RotoWire and ESPN both call Denver's defense stingy, and NBC thinks it is better than the Kansas City loss showed. A Denver-controlled game hurts Lawrence and Tuten together; a Jacksonville blowout helps Lawrence, Little and the defense together.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: The Team 13 trade: Lamar Jackson replacing Lawrence cuts the Denver exposure again. If both the trade and the Golden swap happen, Golden is gone and Tuten comes back into the flex.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Before Sunday 11:00, Mexico City — Golden and Jackson both kick off then
doFirst.title: Send Team 13 the Golden-for-Lamar Jackson offer
doFirst.subtitle: Recomputed today: +26.5 for you, +12.2 for them. Golden's Week 1 makes it easier to sell and more costly to give.

case.label: Their slot column, read today
case.body: Josh Allen starts at slot 0 and is not being asked for. Lamar Jackson sits at slot 20. Travis Kelce is in their RB/WR/TE flex at 178.1; Xavier Worthy is on their bench at 173.9. Golden at 190.3 clears both.

case.label: What you are buying
case.body: Jackson threw for 324 yards and ran for a score in a 41-23 win in which Indianapolis allowed 506 total yards (NFL.com). No injury has been reported for him; his top receiver Zay Flowers is day-to-day with a hamstring Rapoport calls not serious. Baltimore host New Orleans.

case.label: What you are giving, which went up
case.body: Golden led Green Bay with 40 routes and 12 targets, a 28.6% share, and caught 6 for 95 (RotoWire). The strategy file says to buy usage, not sell it, and this is usage. The season field still prices him at 190.3 because it has not moved since August.

case.label: Why it still goes out
case.body: Jackson is a starting quarterback who scores Team 13 nothing behind Allen, all season. For you he is an upgrade at the one position you cannot stream around, and on this week's projections he is 4.7 points better than Lawrence. Golden's 12 targets are also the easiest line in the message.

case.label: The honest risk
case.body: Both sides recompute to the same decimals as Sunday — 2054.0 to 2080.5 and 1969.9 to 1982.1. If Golden's usage holds, you are selling a WR2 for a QB1 on a preseason price, and the flex falls back to Tuten or Lloyd.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: They trade or drop a quarterback, start Worthy in the flex before answering, or Golden posts a second double-digit-target game — at which point his price is higher than this offer and it should be withdrawn, not sweetened.

doFirst.sources: ESPN · RotoWire · Athlon Sports · Bleacher Report · Full Time Fantasy

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Before Sunday 11:00, Mexico City — Golden's game locks first
doFirst.title: Start Matthew Golden in the flex, bench Bhayshul Tuten
doFirst.subtitle: 12 targets in Week 1 against a back with no red-zone work, in a flex that takes receivers.

case.label: The receiver
case.body: Golden led the Packers in routes (40) and targets (12), lined up wide on 92.5% of snaps and caught 6 for 95 with Jordan Love throwing. RotoWire calls him a WR3 with upside at the Jets. Green Bay are 4.5-point favourites.

case.label: The back
case.body: Tuten had 48% of snaps and 15 carries, but Chris Rodriguez Jr. took every red-zone rush and every goal-to-go snap and ran more routes. Denver is a harder spot than Cleveland.

case.label: ESPN disagrees on the third option
case.body: ESPN projects MarShawn Lloyd highest of the three at 11.6, then Golden 11.1, then Tuten 9.4. Reporting sides against Lloyd: he played 30 snaps to Chris Brooks's 37, caught nothing, and Green Bay called it a committee. I take Golden over Lloyd on volume, and the 0.5 projection gap is noise next to 12 targets against zero catches.

case.label: Why this is not the churn the log warns about
case.body: It is a lineup slot, not a roster move, and it reverses the reason this morning's brief benched Golden — which was only that he is the trade chip. Starting a player does not stop Team 13 accepting.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Golden draws fewer than 5 targets at the Jets while Tuten scores from the goal line; or Team 13 accept first, which takes Golden off the roster and puts Tuten back in.

doFirst.sources: RotoWire · ESPN · Yahoo Sports · Heavy · Fantasy Life

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Fallback only · check after 01:00 Wednesday · only if Coker shows FREE AGENT, never as a claim
doFirst.title: If Coker clears waivers unclaimed, add him for Kayshon Boutte
doFirst.subtitle: The only reason he was declined here was the priority cost. A free agent has none.

case.label: Why this is a card now
case.body: The decline on record says do not spend never-resetting priority on a bench receiver. That still stands for tonight's claim. But if no other manager claims Coker, he should become a free agent when waivers clear, and a free-agent add costs no priority at all. Check the status field — if it still says WAIVERS, do nothing.

case.label: The player
case.body: 8 of 9 for 138 and two touchdowns in Week 1, playing through an ankle he called a minor roll; he says he practises Wednesday. He would not start over Rice, Wilson or Golden, but he is a far better bench asset than the seat below.

case.label: The drop
case.body: Boutte, 15.8% rostered: 1 catch on 2 targets, 46% of snaps, behind both Nico Collins and Xavier Hutchinson (RotoWire), with C.J. Stroud throwing. He was added on 9 September, so the seven-day churn window closes before waivers clear. He has no thesis on record.

case.label: The likely outcome
case.body: Coker is 51% rostered nationally and rising. Expect someone in this league to claim him tonight, in which case this card simply expires.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Coker is limited or absent in Carolina's Wednesday practice report — then leave Boutte where he is — or Boutte's snap share climbs past Hutchinson's this week.

doFirst.sources: NBC Sports · Yahoo Sports · RotoWire · Sports Illustrated

action.label: Add Coker · drop Boutte — only if FREE AGENT

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Fallback only · decide on Friday's designation · the drop locks when Las Vegas kick off, Sunday 14:05
doFirst.title: Keep Michael Mayer until Bowers's status is known
doFirst.subtitle: Bowers is still day-to-day. Nothing reported today moves the decision off Friday.

case.label: Where it stands
case.body: Kubiak called Bowers day-to-day on Monday after the meniscus trim and said the Raiders will be smart with him; RotoWire notes a trim usually means closer to a month. No practice report exists yet.

case.label: Why Mayer has more than one week of value
case.body: A Sporting News headline reports the Raiders gave Mayer a $45M extension during Bowers's absence, and ClutchPoints describes Kubiak's offense as one that features two-tight-end sets. IPADE's flex takes a tight end. The Chargers' defense, his Week 2 opponent, looked mediocre to NBC.

case.label: Why this morning's deadline was wrong
case.body: It was set to Friday 22:00 UTC, which is not a kickoff. The drop can happen any time until Las Vegas kick off, so the deadline is now that kickoff.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Bowers practises in full or carries no designation on Friday — then Mayer is the drop before Sunday. If Bowers is limited or out, keep Mayer through Week 2 and read it again next Monday.

doFirst.sources: ESPN · RotoWire · Las Vegas Review-Journal · FOX Sports · ClutchPoints · NBC Sports/Rotoworld

action.label: Drop Mayer — only if Bowers is cleared Friday

whatWentWrong.title: Golden was benched for a reason that was not a reason
whatWentWrong.lead: This morning's roster said not to start him 'into a trade you want accepted'. Starting a player changes nothing about a trade.

case.label: What it cost
case.body: It kept a 12-target receiver out of the flex in favour of a back with no goal-line work, on a roster where the flex takes receivers.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Nothing about the reasoning. If Golden's usage collapses at the Jets, the swap was wrong on the football, not on the principle — see the card above.

whatWentWrong.title: The Coker decline assumed a claim was the only way to get him
whatWentWrong.lead: Waiver players become free agents when waivers clear. The morning brief never checked for that path.

case.label: What was missed
case.body: Every wire player in this file is WAIVERS, clearing at 07:00 UTC. The priority rule governs claims only; the strategy file says free agents are still free. A player nobody claims tonight is addable tomorrow at no priority cost.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: If ESPN keeps these players on waivers past the process time in this league's settings, the Coker card never arms. The snapshot does not show that setting.

whatWentWrong.title: The Mayer card carried an invented deadline
whatWentWrong.lead: Friday 22:00 UTC is not a kickoff or a waiver time. The runbook forbids it.

case.label: The fix
case.body: The deadline is now the Las Vegas kickoff, Sunday 20:05 UTC, and the Friday designation stays in the label as the decision point.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Nothing; it is a correction, not a judgement.

case.label: Their slot column, read today
case.body: Josh Allen starts at slot 0. Lamar Jackson is at slot 20. Travis Kelce fills their slot-23 flex at 178.1 and Xavier Worthy waits on the bench at 173.9.

case.label: Why they say yes
case.body: Golden's 12 targets and 95 yards are the kind of line a manager with a tight end in his flex notices. Jackson returns them zero every week Allen is healthy.

case.label: Why you say yes
case.body: Jackson over Lawrence is +4.7 on this week's projections and +30.9 on the season field, at the position you cannot stream. It also takes one starter out of the Denver game.

case.label: The honest risk
case.body: You are selling the usage the strategy says to buy, at a preseason price, because seasonProj has not moved in three runs. If Golden is a real WR2, this is a fair trade and not a steal.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: They move a quarterback, start Worthy in the flex, or Golden draws double-digit targets again — then withdraw rather than wait.

trades.sources: ESPN · RotoWire · Athlon Sports · Bleacher Report
trades.copyText: Hi — Lamar Jackson is sitting behind Josh Allen and scoring you nothing each week. I'll give you Matthew Golden for him: Golden drew 12 targets and 95 yards in Week 1 and would start in your flex over Kelce. On season projections that's +12.2 for you, and it turns a dead bench spot into a starter. Interested?

worthALook.name: Ravens D/ST
worthALook.lead: Still not worth priority. If nobody claims them tonight, they may be addable for free — and the gap is small either way.

case.label: The matchup
case.body: Baltimore host New Orleans, whose quarterback looked poor in the first half of Week 1 by NBC's read. RotoBaller lists the Ravens first among Week 2 defense pickups.

case.label: Why not
case.body: NBC puts Baltimore and Jacksonville in the same tier this week. A same-tier upgrade is under a point, and the strategy file forbids spending priority on a streamer.

case.label: When to act
case.body: If Baltimore show FREE AGENT after 01:00 Wednesday and Jacksonville have a bad week at Denver, swap them next week at no priority cost. Week 7, when Jacksonville's bye takes your defense, kicker and a flex option at once, is the week this matters most.

doNotChase.name: Chris Rodriguez Jr.
doNotChase.lead: He owns the Jaguars' goal line. It was one carry, and you already own too much of that game.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: Six carries for 23 yards, no target, and one red-zone rush in a 34-10 blowout.

case.label: Why it is wrong for this roster
case.body: You already start three Jaguars at Denver. A short-yardage back with no receptions is the weakest asset in full PPR, and a claim here costs priority you never get back.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Tuten missing time — and even then only as a free agent, never a claim.

doNotChase.name: Tyler Loop
doNotChase.lead: K4 this week. Your kicker is K3.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: PFN's Week 2 board has Cam Little 3rd and Loop 4th. There is no upgrade here at all.

case.label: The pattern
case.body: This roster's kicker slot already reversed twice in two days in early September and the log records it as churn.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Little finishing outside the top 20 across Weeks 2-4 — and then a free agent, not a claim.

cannotSee.label: Whether unclaimed players turn into free agents here
cannotSee.body: The file gives each wire player a clearsAt time but not what happens after it. The Coker card assumes ESPN's usual behaviour — unclaimed players become free agents once waivers process. Check the status field before acting.

cannotSee.label: Priority is one shot and its future value is unknowable
cannotSee.body: Every claim recommendation here is a bet on the rest of the season. The rule that priority buys only an immediate starter exists because the Week 9 injury you will wish you had it for cannot be seen.

cannotSee.body: ESPN returns only your own. Coker is 51% rostered nationally and rising; he will probably be claimed tonight.
